Simulated multi-environment trial phenotypes for the diversity panel

Source: R/genoGWASsim.R
phenoGWASsim.Rd

Phenotypic data for the simulated diversity panel genoGWASraw: a balanced multi-environment trial (MET) with 200 lines evaluated across 6 sites in a 2-replicate randomised complete block design, giving 2400 rows in total. Yield values are generated from a linear mixed model with:

  • Fixed effects. Per-site intercepts drawn from \(U(4.5, 4.9)\) t/ha plus Site:Rep block effects.

  • Polygenic background. TWO Kronecker-structured genotype-by-environment components matching the wgAim multivariate analysis's fa(Site,k):vm(id, K) + fa(Site,k):id decomposition:

    1. K-weighted (trace): \(\mathrm{vec}(\mathbf{U}) \sim \mathrm{MVN}(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{G}_{a,K} \otimes \mathbf{K})\), where \(\mathbf{K}\) is the AlphaSimR-derived kinship (standardised mean diag = 1) and \(\mathbf{G}_{a,K}\) is a \(6 \times 6\) between-site covariance from a Wishart-style construction with mean diagonal \(\approx 0.005\). Kept deliberately small so that once the planted QTL are absorbed as fixed effects the composite genome-wide LRT drops below its significance threshold. Absorbed by fa(Site,k):vm(id, K).

    2. IID line (moderate): \(\mathrm{vec}(\mathbf{L}) \sim \mathrm{MVN}(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{G}_{a,L} \otimes \mathbf{I})\), equivalently each line draws its own MVN(\(\mathbf{0}\), \(\mathbf{G}_{a,L}\)) independently, with mean diagonal \(\approx 0.02\). This is a permanent-environment / line- unique deviation that has essentially zero projection onto \(\mathbf{K}\), so it does not drive the vm(id, K) LRT but keeps the fa(Site,k):id analysis term well- conditioned. Absorbed by fa(Site,k):id.

    Total polygenic variance is \(\approx 0.025\) (\(\sim 18\%\) of residual, giving broad-sense heritability \(\sim 15\%\)). Generating both explicitly matches the classic BLUP decomposition (relatedness contribution + line-unique deviation) and gives each analysis term a clear, disjoint job. A pure \(\mathbf{G}_a \otimes \mathbf{K}\) sim – fine for MVsim's DH-cross interval K with strong block structure – destabilises the fa(Site,k) upgrade with a diversity-panel K (off-diagonal SD \(\approx 0.085\)), because vm(id, K) and id become near- substitutes and their FA loadings compete for the same signal.

  • Residuals. IID Gaussian nugget error at plot level with SD ~0.377 t/ha per site (\(\sim 8\%\) of the trait mean); a simple random Row / Column model in the base LMM is sufficient (no residual spatial autocorrelation).

  • Planted QTL. Five QTL added as fixed contributions to line x site yield values so both univariate and multivariate GWAS analyses have concrete ground truth to recover.

Yields are on the tonnes-per-hectare (t/ha) scale, matching MVsim's scale of ~1. The kg/ha parameterisation used in earlier development was numerically stable in principle but drove REML gradient checks in ASReml close to their default tolerances; rescaling to t/ha avoids those issues without changing any of the analysis results.

The planted QTL (given here in t/ha per allele substitution) sit at realistic breeding-data magnitudes (\(2{-}4\%\) of the ~4.7 t/ha trait mean). Their pooled genetic variance (\(\approx 0.038\) per site across the five loci) dominates the polygenic background (\(\mathrm{diag}(\mathbf{G}_{a,K} + \mathbf{G}_{a,L}) \approx 0.025\)), so absorbing them as fixed effects removes the bulk of the K-shaped signal driving the composite genome-wide LRT. MAIN QTL are sized so that \(|\beta| / \mathrm{SE}_{\mathrm{per\text{-}site}} \approx 4{-}5\) (SE \(\approx 0.03\) t/ha with 200 lines and 2 reps per site), which reliably keeps a truly-constant QTL classified as MAIN by the internal Wald pruning step. QTL 3 is deliberately left small to demonstrate a borderline-detectable effect.

QTLChrcMTypeEffect pattern
1Chr245MAIN\(+0.145\) t/ha across all 6 sites
2Chr590MAIN\(-0.145\) t/ha across all 6 sites
3Chr730MAIN (weak)\(+0.125\) t/ha across all 6 sites
4Chr3110G x E fade\(+0.230\) in Env1 fading linearly to 0 in Env6
5Chr960G x E cross\(-0.180\) in Env1–Env3, \(+0.180\) in Env4–Env6

The corresponding QTL marker names (as they appear in genoGWASraw and mapGWASsim) for the current shipped simulation are SNP_C02_0044, SNP_C05_0094, SNP_C07_0042, SNP_C03_0128, and SNP_C09_0068 respectively. These marker indices are not stable across re-runs of data-raw/simulate_GWASsim.R because the underlying AlphaSimR coalescent samples segregating sites at random – the planted cM positions (Chr2 @ 45, Chr5 @ 90, Chr7 @ 30, Chr3 @ 110, Chr9 @ 60) are stable but the closest well-behaved marker chosen by the sim script can shift by a few indices.

The single-environment (univariate) GWAS vignette uses phenoGWASsim[phenoGWASsim$Site == "Env1", ]. The multi-environment (multivariate) vignette uses all 6 sites with Trait = "Site".

Usage

phenoGWASsim

Format

A data.frame with 2400 rows and 6 columns:

Site

Factor with 6 levels ("Env1".."Env6"). Environment identifier.

id

Factor with 200 levels ("Line001".."Line200"). Line identifier. This column name matches the id column of genoGWASraw and is the natural merge.by argument for gwasAim().

Rep

Factor with levels "1" and "2". Replicate within site.

Row, Column

Integer. Plot coordinates within each site trial layout. Can be modelled as random main effects to absorb row / column trend.

yield

Numeric. Simulated grain yield in kg/ha. Site means and per-site residual SDs vary within the ranges typical of a MET trial.

See also

genoGWASraw, mapGWASsim, gwasAim, primePanel

Examples

data(phenoGWASsim, package = "wgAim")
head(phenoGWASsim)
#>   Site      id Rep Row Column    yield
#> 1 Env1 Line042   1   1      1 3.863112
#> 2 Env1 Line101   1   1      2 4.752622
#> 3 Env1 Line149   1   1      3 4.923626
#> 4 Env1 Line107   1   1      4 4.215916
#> 5 Env1 Line194   1   1      5 4.747395
#> 6 Env1 Line121   1   1      6 4.277532
table(phenoGWASsim$Site, phenoGWASsim$Rep)
#>       
#>          1   2
#>   Env1 200 200
#>   Env2 200 200
#>   Env3 200 200
#>   Env4 200 200
#>   Env5 200 200
#>   Env6 200 200
tapply(phenoGWASsim$yield, phenoGWASsim$Site, mean)
#>     Env1     Env2     Env3     Env4     Env5     Env6 
#> 4.532939 4.764949 4.570196 4.465739 4.717555 4.705073
